clue.text: Backing horse with an appreciable amount

indicators.note: backing tells you the two pieces together are read from right to left

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, as is horse
cum is Latin for with, as in kitchen-cum-diner

explanation.surface: A punter puts a sizeable stake on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns H plus CUM right to left; it is not a bet. Horse and H are both slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: to have a lot of something is to have a considerable quantity.

clue.text: Considers getting to grips with home's unattractive points

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it, so the first word clasps the second

parts.note: someone who muses on a matter considers it
in means at home, as in 'is she in?'

explanation.surface: Someone is weighing up and tackling the ugly features of their house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the drawbacks of a plan are its negatives, the opposite of its pluses.

clue.text: Foreign god elevated in prominent feature in ethnic quarter

indicators.note: in places the turned god inside the facial feature

parts.note: a chin is a feature of the face that can jut out

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Wotan is the German name of the chief Norse god, Odin

explanation.surface: An idol from abroad is raised up on a landmark in an immigrant district.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is the container signal, the second only links to the definition. 'elevated' makes the god read NATOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city district settled by one immigrant community, here people from China.

clue.text: Farm animals of various colours, around fifty held in reserve

parts.note: stock is short for livestock, the animals kept on a farm

indicators.note: around says the colourful word goes round the numeral

parts.note: pied means patched in two or more colours, as in the Pied Piper
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A farmer keeps about fifty multicoloured beasts back from market.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: goods amassed and kept back for future use have been put by as a store.

clue.text: Making 50% reductions, tailor child's exercise regime

indicators.note: cutting each of the next two words by half leaves only its first three letters

explanation.surface: A clothier with a half-price sale adapts a youngster's fitness programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making 50% reductions' keeps the front half of each word: 'tailor' and 'child's' are material, not instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Chinese system of slow, flowing movements practised for health.

clue.text: I must chop pieces at bottom of dog dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the bottom of puts this part beneath the dog

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: to chop something is to cut into it, so the single letter cuts into the pieces

parts.note: men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Someone has to cut up the scraps lying in the dog's bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Chinese meal of fried noodles with meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Hierarchical rule first announced under first pope

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the spoken part below the pope

parts.note: St Peter is counted as the first pope

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so a word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: principal means first in importance

explanation.surface: A pecking-order regulation is proclaimed during the reign of the earliest pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the maxim that in a hierarchy every employee rises to their level of incompetence.

clue.text: Shade reversed in optical illusion

indicators.note: reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trick of the eye shows shadow where light should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pale purple colour, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Unopened eye penned by poet one respected in class

indicators.note: something penned is shut in, so the poet's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet

indicators.note: a word without its opening is missing its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of eye, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A writer of verse describes a closed eye belonging to an admired classmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like authorship, but it means enclosed, as animals are in a pen; 'Unopened' is a closed eye only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the senior and most esteemed woman in a particular group or field.

clue.text: Perverse defender doing badly? Team's boss has only one answer

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the word before it are in the wrong order
having only one answer means the other of the two is dropped

parts.note: a football team's boss is the manager
A is the abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A

explanation.surface: A stubborn full-back plays poorly and his coach can think of just a single solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DOING into DOGIN; THE MANAGER holds two As and 'has only one answer' drops one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from Aesop: someone who spitefully guards what they cannot use so nobody else may have it.

clue.text: Old boy on express entering part of Ireland's capital

indicators.note: entering says the two joined pieces go inside the part of Ireland

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, the part of the island that is in the UK

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means added to the end of the next piece

parts.note: to air an opinion is to express it
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil rides a fast train into Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ireland's capital' suggests Dublin or the letter I, but the phrase splits: the capital wanted is an African one, and 'on' and 'entering' place the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the chief city of Kenya.

clue.text: Banned act top in sport

parts.note: something that is out is not allowed, as in 'smoking is out'
to play a part is to act it

explanation.surface: A prohibited manoeuvre is the best thing in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to top an opponent in a game is to perform better than them.

clue.text: Eg. Panamanian chap in a near miss at sea

indicators.note: someone at sea is confused, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: these fifteen letters are the material

explanation.surface: A man from Panama narrowly avoids a collision on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person from one of the Hispanic countries of the New World.

clue.text: Tipple that comes in pairs?

definitions.meaning: measures of spirits, as opposed to long drinks like beer
a garment with two legs cut above the knee, always spoken of as a pair

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one plural: small strong drinks, and trousers ending above the knee.

clue.text: Complaint from serviceman backed by Republican in us state

indicators.note: in places the two joined pieces inside the state

parts.note: Maine is a state in the north-east of the USA

indicators.note: by means next to, so the politician follows the soldier
backed says the soldier is read from right to left

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics

explanation.surface: A soldier, with a senator's support, lodges a grievance in his home state.
explanation.walkthrough: The complaint is medical, not a grievance. 'backed', 'by' and 'in' build IGR and place it in the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ailment, here a severe recurring headache.

clue.text: Curse devil found with head lowered

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: in a down clue the head is the top letter, and lowering it moves it further down the word

parts.note: to found an institution is to create it
the top letter of the word for found, which drops three places

explanation.surface: A swearing demon is discovered hanging his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is the verb meaning establish, not the past of find. 'with head lowered' moves the C of CREATE down to make RECATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to call down evil on someone.

clue.text: High church from south making no progress

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom up

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
something static stays where it is and gets nowhere

explanation.surface: A lofty church, seen from below, is getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High church' reads as one phrase, a wing of Anglicanism, but splits: 'High' alone is the definition and 'from south' turns only the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone high, in the sense of elated, is in raptures.

clue.text: Indulgence? European in communist city forgetting it

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the communist's name

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian communist revolution of 1917
E is the abbreviation for European, as in EU

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so two letters go from the word before

explanation.surface: A visitor from the Continent in a Soviet town lets a small pleasure slip their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'communist city' is not Leningrad: E goes 'in' LENIN, then 'forgetting it' takes IT out of CITY to leave CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mercy or tolerance shown to someone who might have been treated strictly.

clue.text: Plain member of parliament in saddle?

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the word for saddle

parts.note: to saddle someone with a chore is to land them with it
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so one member is an owl

explanation.surface: An ordinary-looking MP sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' is a noun here, flat country, not the adjective. A group of owls is called a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: a stretch of flat, low-lying country.

clue.text: Shot, or dram, boy's swallowed back

indicators.note: swallowed says the boy's name has taken the drink inside it
back says the boy's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Des is a boy's name, short for Desmond
a dram and a nip are both small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: A lad has knocked back a measure of whisky, whatever you call it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a third small drink beside the dram, but it is the verb, fired from cover. 'back' makes the name SED before it 'swallowed' the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a past-tense verb: fired at someone from a hidden position.

clue.text: Demonstrate upcoming range in home improvements

indicators.note: in places the turned mountains inside the abbreviation

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is the British term for doing your own home improvements

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: the Alps are a mountain range

explanation.surface: A shop shows off its forthcoming line of household goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is a mountain range, not a product line: 'upcoming' turns ALPS into SPLA, which goes 'in' DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to show or exhibit something.

clue.text: National force in a part of Africa suppressing base

indicators.note: in places the single letter for force inside the rest
in a down clue the base is the bottom letter, and suppressing it removes it

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A country's army in one region of Africa puts down a rebel camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun, a citizen of a country. 'suppressing base' drops the last A of GHANA, and F goes 'in' A GHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a citizen of one particular Asian country.

clue.text: Such people deserve respect, primarily in services

parts.note: to warrant attention is to deserve it

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the word for services

parts.note: good offices are services done for someone

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Military personnel of this kind are owed esteem, above all within the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: ranks in the armed services between sergeants and commissioned ranks. 'primarily' gives R, which goes 'in' OFFICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: senior non-commissioned ranks in the armed forces, whom juniors must respect.

clue.text: Girl in resistance initially has trouble getting up

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word after it
in a down clue, getting up means read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in 'without more ado'

explanation.surface: A young woman in the underground struggles to get out of bed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H from 'has' and 'getting up' turns ADO into ODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female given name.

clue.text: In the company of doctor in distress

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the word for distress

parts.note: angst is a feeling of anxiety or distress
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Someone is sitting with a physician who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' belongs to the definition; the lower-case 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a preposition: surrounded by, or in the midst of.

clue.text: Carrier making earlier entry with misplaced aspiration

indicators.note: aspiration is sounding an aitch, so the aitch is said in the wrong place, on the other word

parts.note: old means of an earlier time, as in an old address
a hall is the entrance room of a house
the aitch that shifts from the second word to the front of the first

explanation.surface: An airline gets its application in ahead of time, but with poorly judged ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD HALL said by someone who drops one aitch and adds another: 'with misplaced aspiration' moves the H from HALL to the front of OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large soft bag for carrying belongings.

clue.text: Departs, mad about motorists and their sport?

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: about says the word for mad goes round the motorists

parts.note: someone raging is furious, or mad
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Someone storms off, furious about drivers and the way they treat the road as a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' points back to the motorists, so the definition is a sport for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a motor contest of acceleration over a short straight course.

clue.text: Provocative Kentish couple yet to be identified

parts.note: Kent is the county in the south-east corner of England, abbreviated SE
X and Y are the usual letters for two unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A flirtatious pair from Kent have not been named yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arousing desire, as a provocative outfit does.
